scope_notes: Coverage is against current documented mechanics, including supporting operations and test evidence. Catalog labels for existing unnamed formats do not rename source files or established wire names.

Each named ability, talent and recipe is content within a shared format, not a distinct contract. Specialization combat states are separate because their documented histories and decision loops differ.

Housing, territory construction, sieges, detailed authored maps, racial geography, neutral trade, long offline manufacturing and mandatory voice chat have no current baseline requirements. No contracts are invented for those deferred or absent features.
Quest and world entries cover the documented starter journey, objective tracking, safe locations and explicit transitions. Authored narrative remains deferred.

All 501 original stable entries were examined as connected contracts and all current design questions are resolved. Original names and anchors remain stable. Future content production and runtime evidence remain separately identified implementation work.

Briarwake is the future implementation target. This phase completes documentation contracts only; maps/art, concrete content production, runtime handlers, service deployment and gameplay evidence are separate future work.

review_issues.question: Several class and specialization labels differ from their resource contracts: Grace/Devotion, Soul Threshold/Soul Essence, Maelstrom/Stormcharge, Pact Shards/Authority, and Focus Windows/Aim. Confirm the eventual public terminology without creating duplicate meters.
alternatives: Keep resource-contract labels and map legacy display aliases.
Rename public labels after content review.
review_issues.recommendation: Resolved: standardize public resource labels to Devotion, Soul Essence, Stormcharge, Authority and Aim, following the explicit resource contracts. Marksman Focus remains the separate sustained resource. Preserve stable IDs and one canonical pool per actual resource.
review_issues.impact: Legacy resource labels were renamed across class guidance, ability/talent catalogs, embedded character data and search. No gain, spend, cap or other resource behavior changed. Marksman accuracy behavior remains a separate open decision.

review_issues.question: Minstrel resource contracts use Mana and Harmonies, while Balm Chorus and several talents still refer to Cadence spending or retention. Which references should eventually govern?
alternatives: Mana sustains healing, Harmony is secondary; Cadence belongs only to performance.
Author explicit additional Cadence spending for named Minstrel actions.
review_issues.recommendation: Adopt Mana for sustained Minstrel healing and Harmony as its only specialization meter. Balm Chorus spends two Harmony; Encore of Mercy spends three. Cadence remains the performance resource. Clear Harmony modifies song duration; No Lost Notes reduces song Mana cost using its existing 2% per-rank coefficient.
review_issues.impact: Conflicting Minstrel ability and talent descriptions, embedded copies and class/catalog text agree with the existing three-unit Harmony contract. Runtime handlers still require the shared execution gates.

review_issues.question: Ranger Prepared Retreat and Marksman Steady Distance still refer to accuracy, while the attribute rules and audit retire a random accuracy statistic. Clarify the intended non-random behavior before defining its state.
alternatives: Replace remaining references with deterministic output/positioning modifiers.
Remove those talent effects.
review_issues.recommendation: Replace retired accuracy effects with explicit movement behavior: Prepared Retreat grants one mobile stationary ranged cast after Retreating Step; Steady Distance preserves the final Aim unit during movement.
review_issues.impact: No random hit statistic is introduced. Existing talent IDs, ranks and dependencies are preserved; the selected behavior still needs runtime tests before activation.

review_issues.question: Item grade has an explicit budget role; rarity color is mentioned separately without an authoritative rarity vocabulary. Decide whether ItemRarity remains a separate classification.
alternatives: Keep rarity as separate optional presentation content with an authored vocabulary.
Use grade alone until rarity has a concrete purpose.
review_issues.recommendation: Use grade alone. Preserve ItemRarity as a documented compatibility alias of ItemGrade; do not add an independent rarity field or classification.
review_issues.impact: Item budgeting and acquisition use the existing four grade values. Presentation colors may derive from grade without a second multiplier.

review_issues.question: Clause-based play is documented, but the authoritative clause set and distinction between clause choices and talent routes are unresolved.
alternatives: Author a clause content catalog separate from talents.
Bind clause choices directly to existing talent transformations.
review_issues.recommendation: Use extensible clause records with explicit ruin/shelter/silence output families and targeted finite settlement steps. Talent transformations modify eligible authored clauses and never substitute talent IDs for clause content.
review_issues.impact: Documentation contract complete for Briarwake. Actual clause records, coefficients and handlers remain content/implementation deliverables; the contract no longer leaves the roster model or target semantics undecided.
completion_criteria: Future Briarwake implementation: Author concrete clause content records under the documented ruin/shelter/silence routes, with eligible paid-action tags and exact operations for each of the five progress spends.
Future Briarwake implementation: Implement clause switching and settlement against the single canonical progress store; execute positive/exclusion fixtures before enabling those actions.

review_issues.question: The starter guide must introduce tasks and specialization, but authored story dialogue is deferred. Decide whether this needs a dedicated dialogue format or the existing interaction/tutorial contracts.
alternatives: Use instruction/interaction references for the starter guide.
Author a separate branching-dialogue format later.
review_issues.recommendation: Use the existing instruction_ids and interaction_ids for starter guidance. Branching dialogue, authored narrative and conversation state are outside this contract.
review_issues.impact: The guidance format is settled. Concrete instruction, interaction and starter content remain tracked by world-and-starter-content.

review_issues.question: The combat prose names revalidation_policy; shipped abilities use target_revalidation and timing_policy. Preserve these established references until their relationship is decided. ability_command_v2 remains the exact existing wire-schema name.
alternatives: Treat revalidation_policy as prose for existing target_revalidation checks; timing_policy remains independent.
Introduce a new wire property with a migration.
review_issues.recommendation: Preserve target_revalidation and timing_policy. Resolved targeting composes the former; timing composes the latter.
review_issues.impact: No rename of established ability_command_v2 or shipped JSON keys is needed.

review_issues.question: Combat describes normalized weighting across support providers; the testing chapter describes deterministic ordered marginal attribution. Decide which accounting policy should govern before defining contribution records.
alternatives: Normalized split among support providers.
Deterministic ordered marginal accounting.
review_issues.recommendation: Use deterministic ordered_marginal_v1 accounting in the existing modifier-family order; use stable source, ability and status IDs to order contributors within a family.
review_issues.impact: Combat and testing documentation agree. The accounting preserves one actual damage total and credits only the measured support increment.

review_issues.question: The cycle meter is -3..3, but no authoritative named phase set or phase transition thresholds are specified. Should phase be derived solely from meter sign?
alternatives: Author an explicit finite policy set.
Remove the classification if it is derivable from another contract.
review_issues.recommendation: Derive lunar, neutral and solar solely from the sign of the existing -3..3 cycle meter. Keep cycle_units as the only mutable authority.
review_issues.impact: No phase thresholds or duplicate phase state are introduced.

review_issues.question: Match start/end are implied, but objective, scoring, overtime and phase transitions are not specified.
alternatives: Author an explicit finite policy set.
Remove the classification if it is derivable from another contract.
review_issues.recommendation: Adopt preparing, active, completed and cancelled as the lifecycle. Objective, scoring, overtime and end-condition handlers remain part of an explicitly authored PvP ruleset.
review_issues.impact: The lifecycle vocabulary is complete; duel-and-match-rules continues to block unconfigured PvP execution.

review_issues.question: Wall collision is mandatory to declare, but the set of supported blocking/piercing policies and masks is not specified.
alternatives: Author an explicit finite policy set.
Remove the classification if it is derivable from another contract.
review_issues.recommendation: Adopt stop_on_world with the solid_world semantic mask. Keep single_target versus piercing as a separate actor hit policy; wall-piercing and custom client masks are unsupported.
review_issues.impact: Collision behavior is explicit without prescribing engine-specific layer numbers.

review_issues.question: The ability command example does not specify absent-vs-null aim fields, required character_id, coordinate frame or exact conditional requiredness for every target mode.
alternatives: Require the example keys with explicit null for unused intents.
Allow omission and specify per-mode branches.
review_issues.recommendation: Adopt a fixed three-field input shape with null for unused inputs, optional checked character_id, current-session world coordinates and a complete TargetMode/input-kind matrix. Server content chooses the kind for pet and summon abilities. Reject passive activation and invalid inputs.
review_issues.impact: TargetSelection and the command have structural input branches; command_targeting_errors checks a command against its resolved policy. Visibility, range, floor, session identity and resource checks remain authoritative runtime requirements.

review_issues.question: New symbolic enums, command discriminators, timestamps and identifier namespaces have no established serialized encoding. Which stable representations and compatibility rules will the first actual protocol/database adopt?
alternatives: Explicit versioned string encodings consistent with current snake_case JSON.
Implementation-specific numeric tags with a published compatibility table.
review_issues.recommendation: Adopt exact documented snake_case strings for previously symbolic members while preserving existing serialized values. Use explicit *_v1 discriminators for new boundary messages, RFC 3339 UTC Instant values and contract-typed opaque string IDs. ability_command_v2 retains its established discriminator.
review_issues.impact: Boundary values and compatibility rules are explicit. Adding/renaming a discriminator, changing a field meaning or changing an enum value requires a versioned contract/content revision; unknown values are rejected rather than coerced.

review_issues.question: Which status fields, resource details and attacker identities may observers and affected players receive when a source is hidden?

review_issues.question: The cast lifecycle permits a non-channel start-commit override, but shipped timing_policy tokens cover only release_commit and channel_start_commit. What exact token/semantics will represent that override?
alternatives: Add an explicit versioned non-channel start-commit token.
Constrain initial content to the two existing policies.

review_issues.impact: No unencoded policy is advertised as executable. Interrupted pre-release casts release reservations; committed channel costs are not refunded.

review_issues.question: Does equipping move an instance into an equipment container or retain its bag placement while EquipmentSet owns equipped references? What exact equip/unequip request branch selects the slot?

review_issues.recommendation: Use explicit personal equipment-container placement. Equip and unequip carry one versioned item, quantity one, the slot, expected equipment revision and expected destination-container revision. Atomically update canonical ownership and all slot references.
review_issues.impact: Equipped items occupy no bag slots. Two-handed occupancy is atomic; insufficient capacity for unequipped or displaced items rejects the whole transaction.

conventions: Canonical definitions live only in this registry. The generated schema bundle and HTML are read-only projections. Existing feature HTML and shipped data remain evidence, not alternate contract editors.

snake_case properties follow existing JSON and ability_command_v2. Existing mixed-case keys such as weapon_DPS are preserved for compatibility. Stable inventory IDs and anchors never change when classification changes.

Required means present; nullable permits explicit null. Optional fields may be absent. No implicit default exists. Empty collections mean a known empty set; null means no current selection or applicability as described per field.

Id is an opaque stable string, with a field-level x-reference naming its content definition or instance contract. Content references do not embed live entities. Entity IDs, account IDs, character IDs, item instance IDs and content IDs occupy different namespaces.

Numbers are finite. CombatAmount is measured in domain units with fixed-point thousandths, with final health rounding at resolution. Seconds are durations; Instant is an absolute authoritative timestamp in RFC 3339 UTC (explicit boundary representation; no existing epoch encoding is changed). WorldPoint includes zone, instance, floor and foot-anchor coordinates in authored tile widths.

Currency is integer minor units. No currency name, exchange rate, cap or new currency is introduced. Fractions are 0..1; fields explicitly named percent use 0..100. Existing formula coefficients retain their documented scale.

Arrays preserve order unless uniqueItems and set semantics are declared. Maps are keyed by the referenced stable ID. Runtime collections with unique entities use keyed maps or unique ID sets. No derived display owns a second mutable copy.

Enum encodings are explicit case-sensitive strings. Previously symbolic members serialize as their documented snake_case IDs; existing serialized labels and operation tokens retain their encodings. Never infer numeric ordinals. Unknown enum values or discriminators are rejected. Breaking changes require a new message discriminator and migration; compatible additions require a new package version and negotiated capability.

Static content is versioned by the package content version. Runtime state belongs to the owning world process; durable economic ownership belongs to the transactional service. Client requests carry intent and expected versions, never authoritative results.

A Fully Defined shape is supported at documentation level, not runtime-ready or balanced. Needs Decision schemas validate only their supported portion and cannot certify an unresolved mechanic. Text invariants require future semantic/runtime validation beyond structural JSON Schema.

Reviewed contracts and changed prototype descriptions ship as content package 2.1.0-design; registry format remains 2. ID namespaces are determined by the referenced contract, not a required text prefix, and IDs never authorize access. Session epochs and sequences must never wrap or be reused; acquire a fresh epoch before exhaustion.

A missing concrete map, art asset, deployed provider or executed gameplay test is future implementation/content work. It does not reopen a completed parameterized schema. All required configuration remains explicit; absent bindings/configuration keep future content disabled.
